Linux native desktop validated with GDK_BACKEND=x11 and WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1. Native Wayland failed on this machine; Windows/macOS runners and Apple SDK-derived binding distribution review remain pending.

No live inference, model-quality or GPU-memory benchmark. All agent tests use the actual SDK with an in-process fixture provider. The three existing tuned llama.cpp builds, libraries, 30 weight files and exact profiles/argv are preserved.

Static HTML preview only, with scripts, external resources, navigation and agent IPC blocked. Interactive web embedding, browser automation/CDP and native target integration remain explicit P11 gates.

Local development staging depends on the verified separate reference SDK, its existing dependencies and pinned Node 24.14.0. It is not a standalone installer and does not redistribute the SDK dependency tree, tuned binaries or model weights.

Single warm-cache startup samples and five-minute idle measurements on this Linux display. Builds and occasional manual UI interactions occurred on the same machine. RSS double-counts shared pages; PSS is reported. Short-lived processes between samples and GPU allocations are not fully captured.

Paused-renderer workloads differ: AG1 streams through the real SDK fixture; Dyad holds a running preview with Monaco loaded and no LLM stream. These are bounded-load observations, not a matched provider throughput comparison.

Visual fixtures share viewport/scale/state categories but differ in content: Dyad has an empty chat and split preview; AG1 shows fixture messages and workspace context. AG1 uses an explicit Save/CAS flow and a plain Git diff. No claim of pixel identity or complete A01–A85 parity.

Bridge projections are bounded to recent messages, bounded previews, sequential full approval pages, one executing workspace and at most 32 saved renderer snapshots. Advanced session browsing, terminal-only extension UI and broader mode surfaces remain later parity work.
